transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~51 mins | Recording id ff-20260914-01842
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Polaris CTO), Liam (Polaris Infra), Sofia (Polaris ML), Rakesh (Polaris Security)
---
00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:03 Priya: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:06 Maya: quick agenda, we'll run through current infra, p95 targets, expected concurrency, streaming needs, and then Daniel will do some capacity notes and propose a bench plan. Questions at the end.
00:15 Liam: sounds good, we have limited time so I'll be brief on infra.
00:18 Priya: just to call out, main use case is clinical summarization and triage signals, latency critical for clinician flow. p95 ideally under 600ms for short prompts but we have longer summarizations that can be 8k-12k tokens.
00:33 Daniel: okay when you say p95 under 600ms is that end-to-end or just model generation?
00:37 Priya: model gen plus our pre/post processing, so model budget maybe 400ms at p95, we accept a bit of burst.
00:45 Maya: got it. and concurrency? how many simultaneous clinicians hitting the service in peak?
00:49 Sofia: peak concurrency about 120 active sessions, but each session can stream tokens; average sustained QPS about 45 requests/sec with bursts to 140 for 30-60s during shift change.
01:02 Daniel: ok that's helpful. is streaming required or can you batch?
01:06 Priya: for note-taking and interactive workflows streaming is required — clinicians should see partial tokens within 150-200ms to feel responsive. For nightly bulk summarization we can batch.
01:16 Liam: architecture today: in-house service on k8s, CPU-frontend, GPUs on prem for some heavy jobs. We're evaluating Redwood for hosted to reduce ops and Dedicated for predictable SLA. Private deployment discussed for ePHI.
01:29 Maya: understood. Wrt Private, are you looking for VPC peering or fully on-prem?
01:33 Rakesh: prefer VPC with customer-managed KMS; if that doesn't meet compliance we'll look at air-gapped on-prem option.
01:40 Daniel: Redwood supports both. For VPC we provide a private control plane and you manage KMS/HSM; audit logs are available. For private on-prem, there are additional packaging steps.
01:50 Priya: good. do you have hard numbers for token/sec on different model sizes? we want to size Dedicated GPUs and compare to our infra.
01:56 Daniel: yes, we have token/sec baselines but they vary with sequence length, quantization and KV cache hit-rate. I'll summarize: e.g. for Llama2-13B float16 on A100-like HW, sustained token/sec single replica for generation at 2k context is about 250-400 tokens/sec depending on batching. With our continuous batching and KV caching you can get better tail latencies for repeated prefixes.
02:16 Sofia: hmm our prompts often share long prefixes (patient history), so KV cache sounds promising. how much does cache reduce p95?
02:23 Daniel: in workloads with 60-80% prefix reuse we see p95 improvements ~30-50% on repeated requests because we avoid recomputing attention for earlier tokens. but initial cold calls still pay the full cost.
02:34 Liam: what about streaming latency? if clinician wants first partial token in 150-200ms, can you meet that with Dedicated?
02:39 Daniel: we can with the right instance type and batching policy. The trick is small-batch streaming — we typically route low-latency traffic to small dedicated pools with minimal batching, while placing bulk jobs on high-throughput pools. That said, p95 150ms for first token at 13B is aggressive but achievable for short prompts if tokenization and network hops are low.
02:57 Priya: can you quantify network contribution? We have clinicians on hospital LANs with NATs and a VPC peering setup would be low latency but we also have mobile clinicians on 4G.
03:07 Daniel: network adds variability. For in-region VPC, we aim for <10-20ms network RTT. Mobile 4G can add 100-200ms. So the model and hosting choices focus on model compute + queueing; we recommend co-locating edge gateways in region and using streaming websockets with backpressure.
03:24 Maya: for Dedicated we provide SLA-backed latency targets per model tier. We can map your 400ms model budget to an offering. We'll follow up with documented p95 SLO options.
03:33 Liam: curious about concurrency limits and autoscaling. If we hit burst to 140 QPS for 1 minute, do you autoscale quickly enough?
03:40 Daniel: autoscaling depends on reserved capacity and cold start time. Dedicated can be configured with reserved pods/GPU capacity and burst pools. Cold start for a new GPU replica can be 30-120s depending on model and image warm-up; for that reason we advise a design with headroom (reserve 20-30% during peak) or use warm standby hooks.
03:56 Priya: that's concerning; our shift-change bursts are short. we don't want degraded p95 during that 60s spike.
04:02 Maya: we have burst credit and pre-warming options. For short spikes we recommend dedicated reserved capacity sized for steady + short-term burst. Another option is hybrid: primary traffic to Dedicated, and overflow to Hosted with a slightly higher latency/cost but immediate capacity. Redwood supports policy-based routing for fallback.
04:21 Sofia: what's the cost tradeoff for hybrid? if we pay for reserved GPUs to cover steady and some bursts, plus occasional hosted overflow, is that more expensive than overprovisioning on-prem?
04:29 Maya: that depends, but typically Reserved + hosted overflow is cheaper than 100% overprovisioning because hosted only charges when used. We'll run a cost model if you share traffic traces.
04:39 Rakesh: security question — when overflow goes to Hosted, is ePHI encrypted at rest and in transit? do we lose control of keys?
04:45 Daniel: hosted uses encryption at rest with provider-managed keys by default, but we offer customer-managed keys (KMS) for hosted in enterprise plans. Also data residency options and limited retention policies for inference logs. We'll send the SOC2 and data flow docs.
04:58 Priya: great. another thing: tokenization differences across models — we sometimes see token count blow-ups with certain models causing cost variance. can you help with an eval?
05:05 Daniel: yes, we recommend running a tokenization audit on your sample prompts. We can run the same prompts across target models, measure token counts, p95 latencies and token/sec. That's part of the benchmark template I'll share.
05:16 Liam: about benchmarking — can you run a streaming token/sec test that simulates partial token flushing and websockets to reproduce first-token latency?
05:23 Daniel: absolutely. We'll do two tests: 1) throughput steady-state token/sec with long sequences (8k-12k) to size GPU memory and quantify KV cache benefits; 2) streaming-first-token latency test with varied network RTTs (10ms, 50ms, 150ms). We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token/sec.
05:40 Priya: timeline? we want results before our infra committee review on 2026-09-25.
05:44 Maya: doable. If you upload traces by 2026-09-16 and we run benchmarks on 09-17/18, we'll have a report and cost model by 09-20.
05:53 Sofia: can you include a comparison of quantized model options (8-bit) for Dedicated? we worry about hallucination regressions.
05:59 Daniel: yes, we'll include quantization profiles and recommended evals. For critical clinical outputs we recommend running standard eval sets and Redwood Optimize's quality monitoring to catch regressions.
06:12 Rakesh: last security point — audit logging granularity? we need per-token or per-request traceability for audits and SSO integration with our IdP.
06:20 Daniel: we have per-request trace IDs, user tokens mapping and detailed latency/cost logs. Per-token trace exists in debug mode but is heavier; we can discuss retention and redaction. SSO via SAML/SSO is supported.
06:33 Maya: ok recap: action items and deliverables — Redwood sends benchmark template + price options, Daniel runs micro-bench and streaming tests, Polaris uploads traces and prompts, security docs exchanged and schedule security-specific deep dive next week.
06:49 Priya: that works. thanks everyone. can we lock a 60-min follow-up demo for the actual streaming test results?
06:55 Maya: yes I'll propose calendar times for 2026-09-21 and 09-22.
06:59 Liam: thanks, bye.
07:01 End of recording.
